## Verdict: REJECT (three checklist FAILs at or above the important threshold)

This PR is not ready to merge: three verified checks fail, one against acceptance criterion 13 (the CSV export warning undercounts tagged schema docs), one on dry-run counts with `--clear`, and one on JSON export output that the JSON import parser rejects.

Rule applied: rule 1 — a checklist FAIL at or above the threshold → REJECT

## Code Review Findings

No Phase 3 reviewer raised a new finding at this head. Four reviewers ran: silent-failure-hunter, comment-analyzer, type-design-analyzer and the final pass. Each restated earlier Suggestion-level points without new evidence.

### 🔴 Critical

- VC-86: FAIL (critical) — A CSV export of a store holding at least one tagged record returns `lossy: true` from `export_memories`, and `sqllens export-memory` prints a `Warning:`. Both state how many records' groups were dropped. A CSV import never changes an existing record's groups. [src/sqllens/memory/exporter.py:32-43] — fix the code, or have the issue author amend this criterion

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 13, so it counts. Pair-tagged CSV export works: exporter.py:32-43 csv_groups_dropped_warning counts only SQL pairs with groups and returns 'the groups of N record(s) are NOT in this export'; admin.py:373-376 sets lossy=True and appends it; exporter.py:74-77 appends it for the CLI, which prints each warning with 'Warning:' (cli.py:826). parse_csv (io.py:160-200) builds SqlPairs with no groups, so a CSV import never sets groups. Counterexample: schema docs can be tagged (schema.py:112 SchemaDoc.groups; criterion 8 says groups apply to each SQL pair and schema doc), but csv_groups_dropped_warning (exporter.py:37) never counts them. A store with 1 tagged pair and 2 tagged schema docs exported to CSV states 'groups of 1 record(s)' although 3 records' groups were dropped. A store whose only tagged records are schema docs gets lossy:true and a Warning only from the separate 'N schema doc(s) are NOT in this export' message (exporter.py:69-73; admin.py:367-372), with no statement of how many records' groups were dropped. No sibling criterion narrows this. The count the criterion requires is understated or absent for tagged schema docs.

  </details>

### 🟠 Important / Major

- VC-5: FAIL (important) — A dry run reports the same saved/updated/skipped counts as a real import without writing anything. [docs/external/managing-memory.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Without --clear, dry run and real import share the same plan (importer.py:197-200 computes updated/skipped from _plan; saved increments for planned items at :233 in both modes), so counts match. But with --clear --dry-run, import_bundle calls _baseline(store, clear and not dry_run) (importer.py:197), so the clear is skipped and dedup runs against the existing store. A real --clear import dedups against an empty store, so bundle items matching stored records would all be saved, while the dry run reports them as skipped/updated. docs/external/managing-memory.md:122 itself says the --clear wipe is skipped in dry run, and line 136 says 'reports the same counts' unconditionally, which is false for --clear. cli.py:500 and :521-522 pass clear and dry_run together, confirming the combination is reachable. Real-import per-item save errors also appear only in real runs (importer.py:209-232), though that is secondary.

  </details>

- VC-32: FAIL (important) — export_memories JSON emits each pair and doc via model_dump(exclude_none=True) (docs excluding training_type), so untagged records carry no groups key and the output is accepted by the JSON import parser for round-trip. [src/sqllens/memory/admin.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The first half holds: admin.py:379-388 emits p.model_dump(exclude_none=True) for pairs and d.model_dump(exclude_none=True, exclude={'training_type'}) for docs, so untagged records have no groups key (groups defaults None; schema.py:78,112), and SqlPair/SchemaDoc accept it (extra=forbid, no extras). The second half fails: export writes top-level "sql_pairs" as a LIST (admin.py:381), but parse_json (io.py:135-157) runs MemoryBundle.model_validate(raw) with no normalization, and MemoryBundle.sql_pairs is SqlPairsBlock | None (schema.py:130), a model with a 'pairs' list and extra=forbid (schema.py:96-102). A list value for sql_pairs fails validation, so parse_json raises BundleFormatError on the exported JSON. The admin.py docstring says the shape matches add_memories, not parse_json. The base also exported a list, so this is not new in the PR, but the claim of acceptance by the JSON import parser is false. Requirement: schema.py docstring (unchanged in both views) says JSON round-trips losslessly for import-memory/export-memory.

  </details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (6)

<details><summary>6 items</summary>

- VC-9: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The internal doc asserts a record missing a key matches $ne/$nin/$not_contains, $in/$eq do not look inside lists, and chromadb 1.4.1 and earlier refuse list metadata. [docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Claim is a library-behavior claim (chromadb filter evaluation: missing key vs $ne/$nin/$not_contains, $in/$eq on lists, and list-metadata validation in 1.4.1 and earlier). The item has no dependency_sources, and chromadb source is not in the head view. Doc text read at docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md:113 matches the claim's excerpt. Installed chromadb exists only outside the supplied sources (e.g. .venv site-packages), which I did not treat as an authorized source; no 1.4.1 source is available in any case. Not run: inspect chromadb where-filter evaluation (segment/impl metadata filters, sqlite/hnsw) and validate_metadata for chromadb 1.4.1 vs 1.5.x.

  </details>

- VC-14: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — Spreading group_metadata(groups) into the save metadata produces chromadb-accepted metadata: a non-empty sorted list of strings plus memory_tagged True, or no keys when untagged. [src/sqllens/agent/integrations/chromadb/agent_memory.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  group_metadata (src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py:30-39) returns {} for empty/None groups, else {memory_groups: sorted deduplicated list[str], memory_tagged: True}. It is spread into the metadata at agent_memory.py:246 and :443. Whether chromadb accepts a list[str] value and bool depends on chromadb's validate_metadata. That source is not in the head view (no validate_metadata match) and the item has no dependency_sources. The only installed copy is in the working-tree .venv, which I may not use. Not verified: chromadb validate_metadata and its version.

  </details>

- VC-19: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — sql_key keys a SQL text by sqlglot's MySQL regeneration when sqlglot.parse(read='mysql') yields exactly one non-None statement, so that the regenerated text keeps string literal and identifier case while normalizing keyword case and whitespace; on any exception or zero/multiple statements it falls back to the stripped text. [src/sqllens/memory/importer.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The control flow of sql_key matches the claim (src/sqllens/memory/importer.py:58-64): it filters out None statements, returns ('parsed', statements[0].sql(dialect='mysql')) only when exactly one remains, and on any exception or 0/many statements returns ('text', sql.strip()). sqlglot is pinned at 30.31.0 (requirements.txt:104). The item has no dependency_sources, and sqlglot is not in the views. I therefore could not read the sqlglot parser or MySQL generator to confirm that regeneration keeps literal and identifier case while normalizing keyword case and whitespace. The tests at tests/unit/test_memory_groups.py:320-334 assert this behavior, but I did not run them. Missing evidence: sqlglot 30.31.0 source, or a run of those tests.

  </details>

- VC-69: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The tests reach tool functions via mcp._tool_manager.get_tool(name).fn on the MCPServer returned by build_server, and that fn is the decorated wrapper that turns RuntimeError into ToolError. [tests/unit/test_memory_groups.py]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Repo side verified in head view: src/sqllens/server.py:363-365 registers every tool via mcp.tool(**kwargs)(_tool_errors(fn)), and _tool_errors (server.py:227-234) wraps fn so Exception becomes ToolError(str(exc)). tests/unit/test_memory_groups.py:447-448 reads mcp._tool_manager.get_tool(name).fn. Whether the SDK's MCPServer has _tool_manager.get_tool and whether Tool.fn stores the registered callable as-is (not a re-wrapped one) depends on the installed mcp 2.x library; the item supplies no dependency_sources and the views contain no mcp source, so the library behavior was not read (installed copies exist only outside the views, which I did not use). Missing evidence: mcp/server/mcpserver/tools/tool_manager.py and tools/base.py (Tool.from_function storing fn).

  </details>

- VC-78: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — A record stored before the upgrade, while it remains untagged, is retrieved after the upgrade by requests under every rule set, with no re-import or migration step. [src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py:22,40-47]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Criteria file read; criterion 5 present, so graded with the criteria. Code path traced in head view src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py: an untagged (including pre-upgrade) record has no memory_tagged key; scope_filter() uses {memory_tagged: {$ne: True}} alone for an empty group list, or $or[that, {memory_groups: {$contains: g}}...] for a set with groups. agent_memory.py ANDs this with the existing success/tool_name/is_text_memory filters, and neither write nor migration is needed, so legacy records are selected under every rule set if ChromaDB evaluates $ne on a record that lacks the key as a match. That is runtime behavior of the third-party chromadb library. No dependency_sources were supplied and chromadb source is not in the views, so I could not confirm it from source. tests/unit/test_memory_groups.py:136-182 adds a legacy record without the new keys and asserts it is returned under a set with groups and under an empty scope, but I did not run that test (command not run: pytest tests/unit/test_memory_groups.py against chromadb 1.5.x). Alternative conditions: no selection or unknown rule set gives () which still yields the untagged branch; group_scope None (no rule-set file) applies no filter. Both return legacy records. Verdict withheld only because the library semantic is unverified.

  </details>

- VC-94: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — The `chromadb` lower bound in `pyproject.toml` admits only releases that support list-valued metadata and the `$contains` filter on it, and that evaluate the metadata filter the retrieval uses the way 1.5.9 does for a record missing the filtered key. [pyproject.toml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  pyproject.toml:35 declares "chromadb>=1.5,<2" (head view). requirements.txt pins chromadb==1.5.9. criteria.json is a valid list and carries criterion 21, matching this claim. The claim depends on how chromadb 1.5.0 (the lowest admitted release) validates list metadata and evaluates $contains and $ne for records missing the key. The item has no dependency_sources, and the views contain no chromadb source. The repository only records behavior 'observed on 1.5.9' (docs/internal/setup/preflight.md:76; src/sqllens/_memory_groups.py:17-22 comments). Installed chromadb copies exist elsewhere on the machine but were not supplied as dependency sources, and none was read as a 1.5.0 release. Without 1.5.0 (and 1.5.1-1.5.8) source or a run against them, the claim cannot be settled by reading. Not run: installing chromadb==1.5.0 and checking validate_metadata, $contains and $ne against records lacking the key.

  </details>

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A rule-set file whose rule sets carry `memory_groups` loads with `format_version = 1`. A rule-set file with no `memory_groups` anywhere loads as before this change. A `memory_groups` that is empty, holds a duplicate, or holds a non-string is refused at load like any other invalid rule-set field.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, a `query_database` request under rule set S gets, from both the `search_saved_correct_tool_uses` tool and the automatic system-prompt memory context, only records that are untagged or share at least one group with S's `memory_groups`. A tagged record whose groups S does not list is never returned to a request under S.
- [ ] While a rule-set file is configured, a memory search with an empty group list (the request's rule set lists no `memory_groups`, or no rule-set selection is available to the search) gets only untagged records from both memory paths.
- [ ] A memory search under rule set S returns an in-scope record that clears the similarity threshold even when more records than the search's result limit, all outside S's groups, score higher.
- [ ] A record stored before the upgrade, while it remains untagged, is retrieved after the upgrade by requests under every rule set, with no re-import or migration step.
- [ ] Without a rule-set file, memory retrieval returns tagged and untagged records alike, as before this change.
- [ ] `sqllens verify-memory` run with `--rule-set S` retrieves memory exactly as a `query_database` request under S does.
- [ ] `sqllens import-memory`, the `import_memory` tool and the `add_memories` tool accept an optional `groups` list (non-empty, distinct strings) on each SQL pair and schema doc. An empty or duplicate-holding `groups` is a validation error.
- [ ] An import through any of those three surfaces that names a group no loaded rule set's `memory_groups` lists leaves the store unchanged, with nothing written and, for `sqllens import-memory --clear`, nothing deleted. The CLI exits non-zero and the tools return `isError: true`, and the message names every unknown group. With no rule-set file configured, any import that names a group is refused this way.
- [ ] An imported item that duplicates an existing record or an earlier item of the same import creates no second record and sets the groups of every record it matches this way: a tagged item onto a tagged record gives the union of both; a tagged item onto an untagged record gives the item's groups; an untagged item leaves the record's groups as they were. A duplicate that changed the record's groups is counted as updated, and one that changed nothing as a skipped duplicate. The updated count is shown as `updated=<n>` in the `sqllens import-memory` summary line, in the `import_memory` tool's report, and as `updated_count` in the `add_memories` result. A dry run reports the same counts without writing.
- [ ] Duplicate detection compares `sql` texts with sqlglot under the MySQL dialect: two texts match when each parses into exactly one statement and both regenerate to the same SQL, with string literals and identifiers keeping their case, so `WHERE region = 'EU'` and `where region = 'eu'` do not match while `SELECT a FROM t` and `select a\n  from t` do. When sqlglot raises any exception on either `sql` text while parsing or regenerating (`ParseError`, `TokenError` and `RecursionError` included), or the text parses into no statement or more than one, the two match only when their texts are identical after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, so re-importing the same file still saves nothing new. `question` texts match after collapsing whitespace and ignoring case, and `content` texts match as before this change.
- [ ] For a store in which no two records duplicate each other under the match rule, exporting it to JSON with `sqllens export-memory` or the `export_memories` tool and importing the result into an empty store recreates every record the export wrote, with the same groups, untagged records staying untagged, when every group the export names is listed in a loaded rule set's `memory_groups`. An export naming a group no rule set lists is refused on import like any other unknown group.
- [ ] A CSV export of a store holding at least one tagged record returns `lossy: true` from `export_memories`, and `sqllens export-memory` prints a `Warning:`. Both state how many records' groups were dropped. A CSV import never changes an existing record's groups.
- [ ] `list_memories` and `get_memory` return each record's groups. While a rule-set file is configured, `get_memory_stats` returns the count of tagged records none of whose groups appears in any rule set's `memory_groups`; without a rule-set file that count is 0.
- [ ] `get_access_rules` returns each rule set's `memory_groups`.
- [ ] `sqllens verify-memory` exits non-zero before running any case when its golden file has an item carrying `groups`, and the message names that item.
- [ ] The change leaves these unchanged: with a rule-set file configured, the agent has neither `save_question_tool_args` nor `save_text_memory`; and the memory admin tools (`list_memories`, `get_memory`, `export_memories`, `get_memory_stats`, `delete_memory`, `clear_memories`, `add_memories`) and `import_memory` act on every record for any caller, without regard to rule sets.
- [ ] `docs/external/rule-sets.md` documents `memory_groups` in the file reference and replaces the "Memory is shared by every rule set" limit with the group rule, still stating that the memory admin tools are not limited by rule sets and that SQL Lens trusts `_meta`.
- [ ] `docs/external/managing-memory.md` documents the bundle `groups` field, the unknown-group refusal, how duplicates combine groups, and that CSV carries no groups. Its paragraph beginning "Duplicate entries are skipped automatically" states the new match rule (SQL compared by sqlglot with literal and identifier case kept, exact text when the SQL does not parse) and that a duplicate which changes a record's groups counts as updated.
- [ ] `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` and `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` describe group-filtered retrieval. No doc or code comment states that memory is shared by every rule set as a fact; today that claim appears at least in `docs/external/rule-sets.md` (the "Nothing is saved to memory" and "Memory is shared by every rule set" bullets), `docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md` and the rule-set write-gate comment in `src/sqllens/agent/factory.py`.
- [ ] The `chromadb` lower bound in `pyproject.toml` admits only releases that support list-valued metadata and the `$contains` filter on it, and that evaluate the metadata filter the retrieval uses the way 1.5.9 does for a record missing the filtered key.
